title: Metric Vignette: Model & Route Performance Matrix UI + Chart Specifications
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Design and spec a compact, composable 'Performance Matrix' canvas that surfaces per-model and per-route telemetry for latency, throughput, token flows and cost. The intent is a reusable vignette that can be embedded in route and model detail pages, in rollouts and in the overview list. Deliverables: Figma prototype, high-fidelity chart specs for engineering, interaction notes for drilldown flows (microtrace, request sample), and accessibility/color contrast checks. Focus areas: percentile latency ribbons, throughput over time (TPS), token distribution (prompt/response split), cost-per-1k-tokens, and model-variant comparisons with canary/rollout overlays.
acceptance_criteria: Figma prototype shows a responsive Performance Matrix at 1280px and a compact variant for 920px width
Chart spec includes aggregation windows (1m/5m/1h), retention-aware sampling guidance, and exact SQL/metrics names for engineering (latency_p50/p95/p99, tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_per_token)
Interaction flows: hover tooltip, range-select brush, compare two model-versions side-by-side, jump-to-microtrace and open request sample modal
Accessibility: all charts meet AA contrast and tooltip text is screen-reader accessible
Design sign-off from PM (Ethan Kim) and Eng lead (Priya Patel) and one round of implementation QA checklist passed
tasks: Draft raw wireframe for matrix layout: left column time-series, center token flow, right cost & thresholds
Define chart primitives and variable list (line, area with percentiles, stacked bar for tokens, violin for latency distribution)
Annotate sample data shapes and edge cases (sparse traffic, bursty bots, cold-start latency)
Produce Figma prototype with interactions and overlays for canary/rollout shading
Export chart spec doc (CSV table) with axis units, default time windows, ideal color palette, and legend behavior
Review with console engineering team and update spec with telemetry field names and query constraints
Create QA checklist and provide example Grafana/Timeseries queries for early dev validation

notes_for_engineering: Use latency metrics: latency_ms_p50, latency_ms_p95, latency_ms_p99. Provide both raw and baseline-normalized values for comparison
Throughput: requests_per_min and tokens_per_min. Recommend TPS smoothing at 1m/5m with ability to expand to 1h for longer views
Token distribution: show stacked bars for prompt vs response tokens per request bucket; include an option to normalize by request count
Cost overlay: compute and display cost_per_1k_tokens and rolling cost delta vs previous window
Rollouts: visual overlay for canary percentage and model-variant color banding; ability to switch primary focus between route and model-variant
Sampling guidance: when sample rate < 1%, show 'sampling active' badge and surface representative request samples for KPI debugging
implementation_caveats: Large-cardinality routes should default to an aggregated view and surface a warning before querying full cardinality
Avoid heavy client-side re-aggregation; prefer server-side pre-aggregation for p95/p99 to reduce payload sizes
When returning microtrace links, include stable request_id and timestamp to enable deterministic drilldowns
qa_checklist: Render on model detail page and route detail page (responsive)
Verify percentile bands follow the same color ordering across all contexts
Range-select updates both token-flow and cost panes and preserves comparison selections
Accessibility: keyboard navigation for charts and screen-reader labels for each tile
Data correctness: cross-check chart numbers with raw query outputs for three sample routes
